title: The Battle of Stalingrad
subject: histoire
description: From the summer of 1942 to February 1943, Germans and Soviets killed each other in the ruins of a town on the Volga. Stalingrad becomes the turning point of the Second World War.

hero.hook: In the ruins of a city, the army deemed invincible breaks for good.

blocks.text: From summer **1942** to **February 2, 1943**, the world watches a strip of ruins on the **Volga**, a great river of Russia. At **Stalingrad** (today Volgograd), the German army encountered Soviet resistance ready to make any sacrifices.
With more than **one million** dead, it was the deadliest battle in history...and the tipping point of World War II.

After the failure before Moscow in 1941, Hitler launched , a summer offensive towards the south. The goal: oil from the **Caucasus**. **Stalingrad**, a railway and river junction on the Volga, is initially only a secondary objective. Then the symbol wins: taking the city which bears the name of **Stalin** becomes an obsession. [[Case Blue]]

blocks.caption: Stalingrad in ruins: a merciless urban battlefield.

blocks.text: Hitler was so sure of victory that he reportedly had invitations printed for a victory banquet at the Lux Hotel in Stalingrad.

The German **6th Army**, commanded by General, is diverted to the city. The bombings of the [[Friedrich Paulus]], the German air force, in August 1942 left a landscape of craters... perfect for Soviet defense. [[Luftwaffe]]

The Soviet general **Wassily Chuikov** imposed a simple tactic: stay within **30 meters** of the enemy. Thus, German artillery and aircraft cannot strike without killing their own men. The Germans call it the **Rattenkrieg**, the “rat war”: we fight in cellars, sewers, ruined buildings.

The **Pavlov House**, a building run by a handful of soldiers, resisted **58 days**. In the **Dzerzhinsky** factory, tanks are manufactured under bombs and taken straight to the front. Stalin's **Order 227** summarizes the order: **“Not a step back”**.

sections.title: The pliers that close the trap

blocks.text: While Paulus wears out in the rubble, Soviet Marshal **Georgiy Zhukov** prepares . The German flanks, guarded by poorly equipped allies (Romanians, Italians, Hungarians), gave way. On **November 19, 1942**, the pincers closed: approximately **300,000** men were surrounded. [[Operation Uranus]]
The Soviets broadcast over loudspeakers the ticking of a clock, then a message: a German soldier died every **7 seconds** in the USSR.
Hitler forbids the exit. , head of the Luftwaffe, promises an airlift. He fails. Hunger, typhus, **-30 °C**: the “cauldron” becomes a death trap. [[Hermann Göring]]

sections.title: The surrender that changes the war

blocks.text: On **January 30, 1943**, Hitler appointed Paulus **field marshal**, the highest rank, to encourage him to die rather than surrender. Paulus capitulated on **February 2**. Out of 300,000 surrounded, **91,000** leave as prisoners. For the first time, Nazi propaganda must admit total defeat. The army deemed invincible was broken.

blocks.text: **Stalingrad** (**1942-1943**) annihilates the German 6th Army and shatters the myth of Nazi invincibility, in the deadliest battle in history.
